subject.title: feat(feeds): refresh and manage followed publishers

question: Should OpenClaw core own persistent followed-publisher state, a background publisher-feed scheduler, and the `publisherFeeds.*` Gateway/CLI control plane, or should this remain an external plugin/ClawHub capability behind a smaller generic seam?
rationale: This is a new user-facing control plane with persisted state, network trust handling, and public protocol methods; repository policy routes optional integrations toward plugin or ClawHub boundaries unless core capability is intentionally required.

options.title: Approve a bounded core control plane
options.body: Keep the feature in core only after naming the supported contract, ownership, upgrade behavior, and operator expectations.

options.title: Move publisher-specific behavior outward
options.body: Keep core limited to any genuinely missing generic extension seam and implement publisher following, refresh policy, and UX in an external plugin or ClawHub package.

recommendation.title: Move publisher-specific behavior outward
recommendation.body: Keep core limited to any genuinely missing generic extension seam and implement publisher following, refresh policy, and UX in an external plugin or ClawHub package.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active consolidated proposal and can provide the technical boundary analysis, while the final product decision remains with repository leadership.
